backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 so grad accumulation halves). In a 300 s budget more optimizer steps usually help a small model.

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.3 to keep high LR longer.

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so LR does not decay fully to zero.

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05.

backlog.spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4.

backlog.spec: Raise EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.9.

backlog.spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.008.

backlog.title: Adam beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim 384 with ASPECT_RATIO 64; consider ASPECT_RATIO 96 to keep width 576). Smaller model gets more steps in 300 s.
backlog.title: Depth 6 wider-per-time

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 keeping ASPECT_RATIO 64; test whether larger model wins despite fewer steps.
backlog.title: Depth 10

backlog.spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO = 80 (width 640 at depth 8, a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128) for a wider model.
backlog.title: Aspect ratio 80

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 giving more attention heads; check that dims divide properly.
backlog.title: Head dim 64

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSSL" -- fewer full-attention layers, faster steps (final layer is always full if the code does so).
backlog.title: Window pattern SSSSL

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "L" to test whether full context everywhere beats the speed loss.
backlog.title: Window pattern all L

backlog.spec: If train.py applies a logit softcap (e.g. 15), change it to 30; if none exists, add 15*tanh(logits/15) before the loss.
backlog.title: Logit softcap tuning

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation relu(x)^2 with SwiGLU using hidden dim 8/3*n_embd rounded to a multiple of 64, keeping parameter count roughly equal.
backlog.title: ReLU^2 to SwiGLU-lite

backlog.spec: Shorten the Muon momentum ramp (e.g. 0.85 to 0.95) to over 150 steps instead of the current ramp, or set final momentum 0.97 for the last part of training.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup shorter

backlog.spec: Reduce Muon Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 4 to save per-step time if the count is configurable.
backlog.title: Muon NS steps 4

backlog.spec: Ensure the loss and Adam use fused=True kernels and the training step is wrapped in torch.compile with mode default; remove any per-step .item() syncs (accumulate loss on GPU, sync only occasionally) to increase throughput.
backlog.title: Disable torch.compile dynamic overhead / use bf16 fused ops

backlog.spec: Scale the init std of the token embedding to 0.5 of current (or zero-init c_proj of attention and MLP if not already) to speed early training.
backlog.title: Zero-init projections and smaller init

backlog.spec: If value embeddings are used on alternating layers, restrict them to the last 3 layers to cut parameters and time; otherwise remove them for simplicity and compare.
backlog.title: Value embedding on fewer layers

backlog.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays linearly over the last 70% of the time budget. Leave FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0.0. No other changes.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.7

backlog.spec: Keep WEIGHT_DECAY=0.2 as the starting value for Muon cautious weight decay. Scale the weight decay each step by (1 - progress), where progress is elapsed training time divided by the time budget, so it reaches 0 at the end. Implement this in the same place where the LR and momentum schedules are updated each step.
backlog.title: Weight decay linearly decayed to zero

backlog.spec: Remove the separate lm_head weight and compute logits with the wte embedding matrix (F.linear(x, wte.weight)). Drop the UNEMBEDDING_LR param group. Keep the init of wte as it is, and scale it if needed so the initial logits stay reasonable. This saves parameters and optimizer work. The embedding LR may need to stay at 0.6.
backlog.title: Tie lm_head to token embedding

backlog.spec: For the first 30% of the time budget, train on sequences truncated to half length. Do this by reshaping each batch into twice as many sequences of half the length, with the same token count per step. Then switch to full length. Make sure torch.compile does not recompile in a bad way, for example by marking the shapes as dynamic or accepting one recompile. This should speed up the early phase because attention is cheaper.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum (short context first)

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) after backward and before the optimizer step. This stabilizes the high-LR Adam groups for the embeddings and scalars, and it lets higher LRs be tried later.
backlog.title: Grad clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA copy of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated every step with torch._foreach_lerp_. Before the final evaluation, swap the EMA weights into the model. Do not touch the evaluation call itself. Only copy the weights into the model right before it. Use ema weights only if this is done in the training loop, after training ends.
backlog.title: EMA of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH=4 and ASPECT_RATIO=96, giving model_dim 384. HEAD_DIM stays at 128, so there are 3 heads. Keep the window pattern valid for 4 layers. Depth 8 to 6 helped a lot and depth 10 hurt, so test an even shallower, faster model.
backlog.title: Aspect ratio 96 with DEPTH 4

backlog.spec: Disable the value embeddings and their gates in all layers. Remove the parameters and the code path. This gives a smaller and faster model with more steps. Recent restriction of VE to the last 3 layers hurt, so check whether VE matters at all at this small scale.
backlog.title: Remove value embeddings entirely

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**16 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 64. With grad accumulation gone, the step count roughly doubles again. Set MATRIX_LR to 0.03 to compensate for the noisier gradients. The 2**17 run was only slightly better than the incumbent, so this tests whether the trend keeps going.
backlog.title: Batch 2**16 with matrix LR scaled down

backlog.spec: In the training forward pass only, compute cross entropy with label_smoothing=0.05. Leave the evaluation path untouched, because the harness recomputes val_bpb itself. Make sure the loss function used by the evaluation is not changed, for example by applying smoothing only when targets are given and the model is in training mode.
backlog.title: Label smoothing 0.05 in training loss only

backlog.spec: In the training loop, after loss.backward() and before optimizer.step(), call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0). Keep everything else unchanged. This may stabilize early training at the smaller batch size.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR does not decay fully to zero during warmdown. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "L" so every layer uses full-context attention instead of the SSSL pattern. Check whether the extra context beats the speed cost at this small depth.
backlog.title: Window pattern all long

backlog.spec: For the first 25% of the time budget, train on the first half of each sequence (slice inputs and targets to T/2, keeping the per-step token count constant by using the same batch). Then switch to full length. Use the same compiled model; if recompilation is a problem, mask the loss on the second half instead of slicing. This is cheaper early on and gives more steps.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: Keep an exponential moving average of the model parameters (decay 0.999, updated each step with torch._foreach_lerp_ in no_grad). Just before the final evaluation, copy the EMA weights into the model. Do not touch the evaluation call. Only start the EMA after 50% of the time budget so it tracks the warmdown phase.
backlog.title: EMA of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: Where the training loss is computed with F.cross_entropy, add label_smoothing=0.05 only on the training path. The evaluation path must stay untouched. Test whether it helps the small model's generalization.
backlog.title: Label smoothing 0.05 in training loss

backlog.spec: Change the logit softcap constant in the forward pass (currently 15 in the nanochat-style code) to 30. If it is a different value, double it. This loosens the output range for the lm_head.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 30

backlog.spec: Set SCALAR_LR = 0.25 and ADAM_BETAS = (0.9, 0.95). Both changes are to the Adam groups only, and Muon is unaffected. This tests a gentler update for the per-layer scalars and embeddings.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25 and Adam beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 4 and ASPECT_RATIO = 128 so model_dim is 512 with 4 heads at HEAD_DIM 128. The model is shallower and wider, so it has faster steps and more optimizer updates in 300 s. If the dimension is not a multiple of the head dim, round it up. This is a bolder shape change than before, and it needs checking against the memory limit.
backlog.title: Wider shallow model: DEPTH 4 with ASPECT_RATIO 128

memo:
Helped: changes that give more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s. DEPTH 8→6 (-0.0304, 1.0822/1.0861) and halving the batch (-0.0182, 1.0650/1.0669) were accepted, but both carry a tripwire flag; find out what it means before trusting them. Incumbent mean_adjusted is 1.0660 over 2 runs.

Small gains, rejected: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17 (-0.0044, 1.0616), unembedding LR doubled (-0.0054, replicated 1.0607/1.0604), embedding LR 0.9 (-0.0011), WARMUP_RATIO 0.02 (-0.0004, noise-level), DEPTH 4 with ASPECT_RATIO 128 (-0.0002).

Hurt: DEPTH 10 (+0.0790), removing value embeddings (+0.0149), tied embeddings (+0.0083), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0042), SwiGLU (+0.0028).

Next: 1) Resubmit MATRIX_LR 0.05 with an exact SEARCH match (slot 6 failed to patch). 2) Combine 2**17 batch with doubled unembedding LR, and replicate. 3) Avoid more architecture tweaks (2 accepted, 8 rejected).
